routine patterns of internet use are indicators of psychological well-being and changes in psychological well-being may drive changes in routine patterns of internet uses, particularly in response to major life events, such as a move.
women who report high depression levels decrease Internet communication use, and men with similar depression levels increase Internet entertainment use, following a residential move.

women with high levels of depressive symptoms decrease their internet use for communication with family/friends after moving, while men with high levels of symptoms increase their internet use for entertainment after moving.

how routine uses of Internet communication and entertainment may be indicators of overall levels psychological well-being.
understanding how routine Internet use may serve as an indicator of overall levels of well-being and how changes in Internet use may reflect changes in psychological well-being.
the role of the internet in everyday life and the role that the internet plays in coping with stressful events.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the internet is not a panacea, and is not the only solution for coping with stress and depression.
the Internet is a useful tool in coping with stress, but that the type of coping strategy employed is dependent on gender.

the Internet is a powerful tool for communication and entertainment, and that it can serve as a useful coping mechanism in the event of major life changes, especially in the form of residential moves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Internet serves as a coping mechanism for individuals who are experiencing a major life event.
Internet use for communication is associated with positive psychological well-being and that Internet use for entertainment is associated with negative psychological well-being.
Internet use is a coping strategy for women, while for men it is a way of dealing with boredom.
The main takeaway from our work is that
routine uses of the internet for communication and entertainment are indicators of overall levels psychological well-being.
the Internet can serve as a tool to help people maintain their psychological well-being, and that the Internet may be used to help people cope with stressful life events.
the routine patterns of Internet use that we see in everyday life are not random, but are instead related to our psychological well-being.
